newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL - CELTICS NAME HEAT PERSONNEL DIRECTOR WALLACE AS GM.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL - CELTICS NAME HEAT PERSONNEL DIRECTOR WALLACE AS GM.

text.p: The Boston Celtics took another step in their overhaul from the worst season in the history of the storied franchise by tabbing Miami Heat director of player personnel Chris Wallace on Tuesday as their general manager.
As compensation for Wallace, the Heat swapped second-round picks with Boston in the June NBA draft. Miami will now have the first choice of the second round, the 30th overall choice.
The 38-year-old Wallace signed a three-year contract at undisclosed terms.
Boston coach and team president Rick Pitino, who left the University of Kentucky earlier this month to steer the Celtics, is charged with rebuilding from a 15-67 record from this season.

"This (being a GM) has been a goal of mine for a long time," said Wallace. "I've been enamoured with Rick and his style for many, many years. And it's something I wanted to do, I wanted to work on the Rick Pitino team.
"I'm a big Jimmy Johnson fan, I think Rick is going to be the Jimmy Johnson of the NBA, a guy coming out of the college ranks with a fresh approach, a demanding coach, but a fair coach.
"A coach that's going to be very creative in looking down all the avenues available for us to replenish the talent stock of this franchise."
Said Pitino: "I wanted someone who could do everything he could humanly possibly do to take on a team that has won 15 games. There's only one person I had in mind, and that was Chris Wallace."
Wallace, who is well-versed in scouting college players, was also in charge of evaluating players on all levels, from the NBA to CBA as well as international players for the Heat.

"It didn't look like it was going to work out at first, but we pursued it even harder," added Pitino. "I knew we had to give up the 30th pick overall, but I actually think he's worth a couple of first-round picks, that's how valuable he is."
Wallce has spent the last four seasons with the Heat and has also worked for the Portland Trail Blazers, Denver Nuggets, Los Angeles Clippers and New York Knicks.
